title: GARM / Fleet Overview
description: Health, capacity and demand for the whole GARM deployment.

panels.title: Controller
panels.description: garm_health. UP when the controller is serving.

panels.title: Idle runners
panels.description: Runners registered and waiting for jobs.

panels.title: Queued jobs
panels.description: Jobs waiting for a runner. Sustained growth means demand exceeds capacity.

panels.title: Jobs (24h)
panels.description: Jobs completed in the last 24 hours.

panels.title: Dropped events
panels.description: Database change notifications dropped on watcher backpressure. Any nonzero value means internal caches may be stale — investigate.

panels.title: Runners by instance status
panels.description: Provider-side instance states across the whole fleet.

panels.title: Runners by runner status
panels.description: Forge-side runner states (idle/active/installing/...) across the fleet.

panels.title: Pool utilization (top 15)
panels.description: Runner count relative to max_runners per pool. Persistently red pools are capacity-starved; consider raising max_runners.

targets.expr: topk(15, count by (pool_id) (garm_runner_status{pool_id!=""}) / on(pool_id) group_left() label_replace(garm_pool_max_runners, "pool_id", "$1", "id", "(.+)"))

panels.title: Runner lifecycle events
panels.description: Why runners are being removed. A spike in bootstrap_timeout usually means a broken image/network/userdata; provider_error points at the IaaS.

panels.title: Provider operations
panels.description: Successful provider operations per second, by provider and operation.

panels.title: GitHub API rate limit remaining
panels.description: Remaining API budget per credential. Alert before this hits zero — an exhausted credential stalls all reconciliation for its entities.
